Russia Ionospheric Disturbance and Weaponization Program 

#ufo #ufotwitter 

Way to actively disturb or perturb the ionosphere (the upper atmospheric layer rich in charged particles) by injecting high-speed jets of vapor from a plasma-forming substance (e.g., aluminum) into it. The idea is to create localized regions of ionized gas at high altitudes in a controlled way.

Patent RU2144685C1 – “Method to disturb ionosphere and gear for its implementation”

Inventors & Assignee

Inventors: V.V. Adushkin, Yu.I. Zetser, N.I. Zotov, Yu.N. Kiselev, B.D. Khristoforov, V.L. Yuryev, Yu.V. Poklad.

Original Assignee: Институт динамики геосфер РАН (Institute of Geosphere Dynamics of the Russian Academy of Sciences).

What the Invention Describes

1. Method (Core Idea)

It proposes a way to actively disturb or perturb the ionosphere (the upper atmospheric layer rich in charged particles) by injecting high-speed jets of vapor from a plasma-forming substance (e.g., aluminum) into it. The idea is to create localized regions of ionized gas at high altitudes in a controlled way.

Parameters such as jet energy and mass are chosen so they efficiently interact with the ionosphere and produce strong ionization effects without overlap between jets.

2. Implementation Gear / Device

The patent also describes a device to carry out this method, involving:

Explosive charges with shaped cavities lined or filled with the plasma-forming substance.

Initiation and control means for releasing these jets at high altitude.

After detonation, the explosive vaporizes the plasma-forming material and ejects it at high speed into the ionosphere, where it rapidly ionizes and heats surrounding air.

Purpose or Effect

The stated purpose is to enable active experimental exploration of the ionosphere — generating ionized regions larger and with different characteristics than those produced by natural phenomena (like solar UV radiation or explosions alone).

This could help researchers observe ionospheric responses and properties in controlled perturbations.

From a purely technical standpoint, anything that manipulates the ionosphere could theoretically affect:

Radio communications

Radar systems

GPS signals

Over-the-horizon military communication

DTIC-Unclassified document from December 30, 1968 on the USSR/Russia Ionosphere Modification

The document focuses on how nuclear bursts (especially at high altitudes) artificially modify the ionosphere — creating intense ionization, plasma clouds, electromagnetic disturbances, and changes to radio-wave propagation. It draws heavily from Soviet publications, as well as their analyses of American high-altitude nuclear tests (notably Projects Argus and Starfish Prime / Operation Fishbowl in 1958 and 1962).

Topics Covered

USSR Nuclear War Doctrine — Soviet views on the inevitability of nuclear conflict and strategic implications of ionospheric disruption.

Soviet Ionospheric Research — Historical development and organizational structure in the USSR.

Physical Effects of High-Altitude Nuclear Bursts — Ionization levels, plasma expansion, artificial auroras, magnetic field disturbances, and shock wave propagation in the atmosphere. Includes theoretical models (e.g., Leypunskiy's magnetic dipole model for plasma behavior and Rayzer's similarity solutions for shock waves).

Impacts on Military Systems:

Severe disruption of shortwave (HF), mediumwave (MF), and low-frequency communications.

Radar blackout or jamming.

Effects on satellites and electronic equipment (including radiation damage to detectors and semiconductors).

Electromagnetic pulse (EMP)-like phenomena.

Radio-Wave Propagation in Disturbed Ionized Regions — How artificially created plasma clouds affect signal transmission, reflection, and absorption.

Soviet Monitoring/Analysis — Detailed Soviet observations and interpretations of U.S. tests like Argus (artificial radiation belts) and Starfish Prime (widespread ionospheric and radio effects).

Report highlights Soviet interest in high-altitude nuclear bursts as a potential military tool — capable of creating widespread, long-lasting communication blackouts, degrading enemy radar/electronics, and supporting surprise attack strategies in nuclear scenarios. It notes specific quantitative estimates, such as electron densities reaching ~10⁷ electrons/cm³ from a 1-megaton burst at certain altitudes.

China And Russia Have Run Controversial Experiments That Modified Earth's Atmosphere

There is news from 2018 of Russia-China joint venture that conducted a controversial series of experiments to modify Earth's atmosphere with high-frequency radio waves.
